intent.raw_query: Montreal food and festivals, $1500 solo, 4 days, July 2027, from Toronto

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and artisan foods. Chat with local vendors and discover seasonal specialties unique to Montreal's culinary scene.

experiences.name: Montreal International Jazz Festival
experiences.description: Attend one of the world's largest jazz festivals held annually in late June to early July. Enjoy dozens of free outdoor stages and affordable ticketed indoor shows featuring local and international artists across multiple genres beyond jazz.

experiences.name: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal, stopping at local poutine spots, bagel vendors, and classic Quebecois bistros. Discover the historic architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier while indulging in authentic local flavors.

experiences.name: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Stroll
experiences.description: Experience the vibrant local culture of the Plateau by joining one of its many neighbourhood street festivals. Enjoy live music, local artisan vendors, food trucks serving Quebecois comfort food, and the bohemian atmosphere of Montreal's most iconic residential district.

experiences.name: St-Laurent Boulevard Culinary Crawl
experiences.description: Walk the legendary 'Main' from Chinatown through the Plateau, tasting smoked meat sandwiches at local delis, Portuguese grilled chicken, and classic Montreal-style bagels fresh from the wood-fired oven at iconic spots like Schwartz's and St-Viateur Bagel.
experiences.location: Boulevard Saint-Laurent, Mile End to Plateau

trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the morning flight time to rest and prepare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Old Montreal Stay, then take a self-guided walk through Old Montreal's cobblestone streets. Visit Place Jacques-Cartier, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free), and soak in the historic waterfront along the Old Port. Get oriented with your neighbourhood before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — Join an evening stroll through the historic quarter stopping at local poutine spots and bagel vendors. This is the perfect low-key, affordable introduction to Montreal's street food culture right on your doorstep.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at Montréal-Trudeau Airport before landing.
meals.lunch: After check-in, grab a classic Montreal-style poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal outpost or a nearby casse-croûte (snack bar) — expect to pay around $10–14 CAD.
meals.dinner: During the Street Food Walk, sample budget bites: a fresh Montreal bagel with cream cheese (~$3–5), a small poutine (~$10), and a local craft lemonade. Total dinner spend: ~$15–20 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight arrives at 13:00, allow 1.5–2 hours for baggage, transit, and hotel check-in before starting afternoon activities. The STM metro and bus system is very affordable ($3.75/ride or a 3-day pass for ~$21 CAD). Old Montreal is very walkable from your hotel — no transit needed for Day 1 activities.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the metro (Orange Line to Jean-Talon station) to explore one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, seasonal summer fruits, artisan bread, and charcuterie. Arrive early (9:00–10:00) to beat crowds and get the freshest picks at the best prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot. Browse the colourful murals on rue Saint-Denis, window-shop the quirky boutiques on avenue du Mont-Royal, and relax in Parc Lafontaine — a beautiful free green space popular with locals. Rent a BIXI bike (~$7/30 min or a day pass for ~$15 CAD) to cover more ground affordably.
day_by_day.evening: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Stroll — Many local street festivals run throughout July in the Plateau. Join the lively evening atmosphere with live music, local artisan vendors, and community food stalls. This is quintessential Montreal summer culture at its most authentic and free.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh croissant and café au lait from a local boulangerie near Old Montreal (~$5–7 CAD) before heading to Jean-Talon.
meals.lunch: Graze at Jean-Talon Market itself — assemble a picnic of local cheese, bread, cured meats, and seasonal fruit for around $12–16 CAD total. Eat at the market's communal benches.
meals.dinner: Dine at a casual BYOB (Apportez votre vin) restaurant on the Plateau — Montreal is famous for affordable BYOBs. Try Au Petit Extra or a similar neighbourhood bistro for a 2-course meal around $18–25 CAD. Grab a bottle of wine from a nearby SAQ or dépanneur (~$12–15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is open daily in summer, typically 7:00–18:00. The metro ride from Old Montreal (Champ-de-Mars or Place-d'Armes station) to Jean-Talon is straightforward on the Orange Line — about 25 minutes. Check local event listings on MTL.org for specific Plateau festival dates and locations.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or walk up Mont Royal Park — Montreal's iconic green mountain offers stunning panoramic views of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River. The park is completely free. Follow the main trail to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout (about 45–60 min walk up). Bring water and sunscreen — highs around 25°C.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal International Jazz Festival — Although the main festival runs late June to early July, check the 2027 schedule as programming sometimes extends into mid-July with free outdoor stages. Head to the Quartier des Spectacles (easily walkable or a short metro ride from Old Montreal). Dozens of free outdoor concerts run throughout the day on multiple stages. Arrive by 14:00 to catch afternoon sets.
day_by_day.evening: Continue at the Montreal Jazz Festival for the prime evening performances. The free outdoor main stages typically feature headline acts from 18:00–22:00. Grab street food from festival vendors and enjoy world-class live music under the summer sky — one of the best free entertainment experiences in the world.

meals.breakfast: Cook simple breakfast at the hotel if facilities allow, or visit a local dépanneur (corner store) for yogurt, fruit, and coffee — budget ~$5–8 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack a light picnic from a nearby IGA or Marché 440 supermarket before heading to Mont Royal (~$8–12 CAD). Eat at the summit with a view.
meals.dinner: Eat from Jazz Festival street food stalls — look for vendors selling local specialties like smoked meat sandwiches (~$12), corn on the cob, and Québécois crepes (~$8–10). Budget $18–22 CAD for a satisfying festival dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the 2027 Montreal Jazz Festival exact dates at montrealjazzfest.com — the festival typically spans 11 days. Even if the official festival has ended, the Quartier des Spectacles hosts free outdoor events all summer long. Mont Royal Park is a 20-minute walk from downtown or take bus 11 from Mont-Royal metro station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Marché Atwater — a second beloved Montreal market, smaller and more intimate than Jean-Talon, located along the Lachine Canal. Browse local produce, Quebec specialty foods, and artisan goods. Walk or cycle along the scenic Lachine Canal path (free BIXI docking stations nearby) for a beautiful morning along the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Old Montreal for a final leisurely afternoon. Visit the free archaeological crypt under Place d'Youville, explore the historic Pointe-à-Callière Museum exterior, and browse the artisan craft stalls along the waterfront. Spend time at the Old Port waterfront, watching street performers and enjoying the summer atmosphere. Consider a free visit to the public beach at Plage de l'Horloge if open.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner and farewell evening in Old Montreal. Stroll rue Saint-Paul — Montreal's oldest street — for last souvenir shopping at budget-friendly stores. End the trip with a classic Montreal smoked meat sandwich or a bowl of authentic poutine at a local institution.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Montreal breakfast at Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal or a similar local café — eggs, toast, and coffee for ~$14–18 CAD. A slight splurge for the last day.
meals.lunch: Picnic along the Lachine Canal using fresh goods from Atwater Market — bread, cheese, local charcuterie, and seasonal fruit for ~$12–15 CAD. Eat by the water.
meals.dinner: Classic farewell dinner at Schwartz's Deli (famous smoked meat sandwiches, ~$12–16 CAD) or Chez Ma Grosse Truie Chérie for authentic poutine (~$13 CAD). Add a local Unibroue craft beer (~$7) for a true Quebec send-off. Total: ~$20–25 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Atwater Market is open daily in summer, 8:00–18:00, and is reachable via the Lionel-Groulx metro station (Green or Orange Line). The Lachine Canal cycling path is flat, scenic, and perfect for a leisurely morning ride. If departing Montreal on July 18, plan checkout and any airport transfers accordingly — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before any flight departure from YUL.

trip_options.title: Classic Montreal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and artisan foods. Chat with local vendors and discover seasonal specialties unique to Montreal's culinary scene.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Travel from airport to Old Montreal hotel via taxi or 747 express bus (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a self-guided walk along Rue Saint-Paul and Place Jacques-Cartier to soak in the cobblestone atmosphere near your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Wander the historic cobblestone streets of Old Montreal, stopping at local poutine spots, bagel vendors, and street food stalls. Explore landmarks like Notre-Dame Basilica exterior, the Old Port waterfront, and Bonsecours Market. This neighbourhood-level exploration is perfect as a gentle first-afternoon activity right from your hotel doorstep.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River. Enjoy the warm summer evening with a cold local craft beer from a terrasse patio. Wind down with a relaxed dinner before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arriving at 13:00 means lunch is the first real meal.
meals.lunch: L'Gros Luxe (Old Montreal) — casual, affordable comfort food with a local twist; try their loaded poutine and a local micro-brew. Budget ~$18–22 CAD.
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — mid-range seafood and Québécois comfort food in a lively, dimly lit bistro setting. Budget ~$45–60 CAD per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally lighter given the 13:00 arrival. Old Montreal is walkable from your hotel so no transit needed. Pick up a rechargeable OPUS card at the airport for easy metro and bus access throughout the trip. Weather should be warm (~25°C) — light layers recommended for evening.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line north to Jean-Talon station, ~25 min from Old Montreal) to explore one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh berries, charcuterie, and artisanal breads. Arrive early (~9:30 AM) to beat the midday crowds and get the best selection from vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Culinary Crawl: Head to the legendary 'Main' — Boulevard Saint-Laurent — and walk from Chinatown through the Plateau neighbourhood. Taste smoked meat sandwiches (a Montreal must), Vietnamese bánh mì, Portuguese chicken, and local pastries. This stretch is a living cross-section of Montreal's multicultural food identity. Walk south-to-north for a natural progression through the city's culinary history.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal International Jazz Festival: Head to the Quartier des spectacles (metro Place-des-Arts, ~10 min from Old Montreal) for an evening of world-class jazz. Many outdoor stages are free — check the festival schedule for headliner times. Enjoy the electric atmosphere of thousands of music lovers on a warm July night.

meals.breakfast: At Jean-Talon Market — graze on fresh pastries, a maple latte from a market vendor, and a slice of local cheese. Budget ~$10–15 CAD.
meals.lunch: Schwartz's Deli on St-Laurent — iconic Montreal smoked meat sandwich with a pickle and cherry cola. A true bucket-list Montreal meal. Budget ~$20–25 CAD.
meals.dinner: Grab casual bites near the Jazz Festival grounds — food trucks and pop-up vendors offer poutine, crêpes, and grilled corn. Budget ~$20–30 CAD, keeping it light and festive.

day_by_day.notes: The Jazz Festival typically runs late June to early July — confirm exact 2027 dates in advance, as the festival may be winding down or have a special late-season event. Even if the main festival has ended, the Quartier des spectacles often hosts summer outdoor events. Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekends — a Thursday visit is a sweet spot for a relaxed experience.

day_by_day.morning: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Stroll: Head to the Plateau — Montreal's most characterful neighbourhood — to experience its vibrant local culture. Friday mornings often feature local market stalls, street musicians, and neighbourhood activity on Rue Rachel and around Parc Lafontaine. Pick up fresh fruit, local honey, or artisan goods from pop-up vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Parc du Mont-Royal — Montreal's beloved 'mountain' park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of the city skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Rent a rowboat on Lac aux Castors or simply relax on the grass. This is the perfect mid-trip breath of fresh air before another food-focused evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Montreal for a leisurely evening. Explore Rue Notre-Dame and Rue Saint-Paul for boutique shopping and gallery browsing, then settle in for a long, indulgent dinner at a Québécois restaurant — the classic Friday-night experience in Montreal.

meals.breakfast: Café Larue & fils (Plateau) — beloved local café known for excellent espresso, avocado toast, and fresh-baked goods. Budget ~$15–20 CAD.
meals.lunch: Au Pied de Cochon (Plateau) — world-famous for decadent Québécois cuisine including duck confit poutine and foie gras dishes. A splurge-worthy mid-range lunch. Budget ~$35–50 CAD.
meals.dinner: Chez l'Épicier (Old Montreal) — creative market-driven cuisine in an intimate bistro setting steps from your hotel. Excellent tasting menus and local wine pairings. Budget ~$55–70 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Mont-Royal — the main lookout is a moderate uphill walk (~30 min). Bring a water bottle and sunscreen given the 25°C summer weather. Check local event listings for any Friday evening neighbourhood festivals or outdoor cinema events in Parc Lafontaine.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Jean-Talon Market on a Saturday for the full weekend market experience — significantly more vendors, live music, and a festive atmosphere compared to weekdays. Stock up on Quebec maple syrup, local jams, or artisan cheeses as edible souvenirs to bring home. Chat with farmers and producers directly about their products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Neighbourhood Exploration: Walk or bike through the trendy Mile End district — home to Montreal's famous St-Viateur Bagel shop (wood-fired, hand-rolled bagels, a Montreal institution), indie coffee shops, murals, and boutiques along Rue Bernard and Avenue Laurier. This is the creative, bohemian heart of the city and a wonderful final-afternoon discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening back in Old Montreal — enjoy a sunset aperitif on a rooftop or waterfront terrasse, then a celebratory farewell dinner. Browse the lit-up cobblestone streets one last time and pick up any last-minute local gifts from the Marché Bonsecours artisan shops.

meals.breakfast: St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) — get a fresh-from-the-oven sesame or poppy seed bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon. A Montreal ritual. Budget ~$8–12 CAD.
meals.lunch: Lawrence Restaurant (Mile End) — beloved neighbourhood brunch and lunch spot with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. Try the weekend brunch menu. Budget ~$25–35 CAD.
meals.dinner: Olive & Gourmando (Old Montreal) — charming, warmly lit bistro-café known for creative sandwiches, salads, and hearty mains. Perfect relaxed final dinner near the hotel. Budget ~$30–45 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the best day for markets and neighbourhood life in Montreal — embrace the slower, festive weekend pace. If departing the next morning, pack bags the night before. Mile End to Old Montreal is about 6 km — consider renting a BIXI bike (Montreal's public bike-share) for a scenic ride back through the Plateau and downtown. A perfect final-day activity that combines exercise, sightseeing, and local culture.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Montreal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and artisan foods. Chat with local vendors and discover seasonal specialties unique to Montreal's culinary scene.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Montreal Stay via private luxury car service. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk: Embark on a guided premium walking tour through the historic quartier, discovering hidden courtyards, sampling artisan poutine, Montreal-style bagels, and local charcuterie from curated vendors along Rue Saint-Paul and Place Jacques-Cartier. The warm 25°C summer weather makes this an ideal first immersion into the city.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Old Montreal fine-dining restaurant, followed by a relaxed evening walk along the illuminated Vieux-Port waterfront. Enjoy the golden-hour light over the St. Lawrence River from the Quai de l'Horloge promenade.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival; grab a light snack at the airport or upon landing.
meals.lunch: Light bites during the Old Montreal Street Food & History Walk — artisan poutine, smoked meat croquettes, and local cheese tastings included in the premium tour experience.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — One of Montreal's most iconic fine-dining institutions, Chef Normand Laprise's flagship restaurant on Place Jean-Paul-Riopelle. Expect a seasonal tasting menu showcasing the finest Quebec produce, foie gras, and locally sourced seafood. Reserve well in advance. (~$150–$200 CAD per person, wine pairing available.)

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 13:00 — allow 60–90 minutes for baggage claim, customs, and private transfer to Old Montreal. Book airport transfer in advance through a luxury car service such as Limousine Royal or Montreal Limo. Confirm hotel check-in time and request early luggage storage if needed. Weather will be warm and sunny — light summer attire recommended for the afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take a chauffeured ride to the Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie neighbourhood for a premium guided tour of Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest and most vibrant open-air markets. Sample award-winning Quebec cheeses (including Oka and Comtomme), artisan maple products, fresh heritage tomatoes, local charcuterie, and freshly baked pastries from top vendors. A private guide will curate the experience with insider access to the best stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Culinary Crawl: Head to the legendary 'Main' for a curated premium culinary crawl from Chinatown through the Plateau-Mont-Royal. Taste world-class smoked meat sandwiches at Schwartz's Deli, Vietnamese bánh mì, artisan ice cream, and craft beverages at carefully selected stops. A knowledgeable local guide provides cultural and historical context along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal International Jazz Festival: Head to the Quartier des Spectacles for a spectacular evening at the world-renowned Jazz Festival. Enjoy ticketed premium indoor performances at Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier or Club Soda featuring headline international jazz artists, alongside the free outdoor stage performances in the festive plaza atmosphere. The warm summer evening is perfect for outdoor concert enjoyment.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Olive + Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved artisan bakery-café known for its housemade granola, smoked salmon tartines, and exceptional espresso. (~$25–$35 CAD per person.)
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the St-Laurent Culinary Crawl. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost offers an elegant French-inspired seasonal menu in a stunning garden terrace setting. (~$80–$120 CAD per person.)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Restaurant Helena on Saint-Jacques Street — a sophisticated Mediterranean-inspired restaurant known for its whole roasted fish, premium steaks, and exceptional wine list. Perfect for a refined meal before the Jazz Festival evening. (~$100–$150 CAD per person.)

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest mid-morning — arrive by 9:30 AM for the best experience. Book the premium food tour guide in advance through a service like Fitz & Follwell or a bespoke concierge. Check the Jazz Festival schedule in advance at montrealjazzfest.com and purchase VIP or premium indoor concert tickets early as headline shows sell out quickly. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the culinary crawl — St-Laurent is a long boulevard.

day_by_day.morning: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Stroll: Spend the morning exploring the bohemian, art-filled streets of the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood. Join a local neighbourhood street festival or cultural market (the Plateau hosts numerous summer weekend events). Browse independent boutiques on Avenue Mont-Royal, admire the famous outdoor staircases and vibrant murals, and soak in the authentic local Montréalais lifestyle. Stop at a local café for a mid-morning break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mont Royal Park Luxury Picnic & City Views: Arrange a premium gourmet picnic through your hotel concierge (charcuterie, Quebec cheeses, chilled rosé, artisan breads, and seasonal fruits) and hike or take a calèche (horse-drawn carriage) to the Kondiaronk Belvedere summit lookout for panoramic views of the Montreal skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Spend a relaxed afternoon enjoying the park's natural beauty in the warm summer weather.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Montreal International Jazz Festival for a second evening of world-class performances. This time, explore the outdoor free stages for a more festive, communal atmosphere before settling into a premium ticketed late-night club performance featuring a headline jazz or blues act.

meals.breakfast: Le Cartet in Old Montreal — a beloved gourmet épicerie and café serving exceptional breakfast boards with local cheeses, cured meats, house-baked bread, and specialty coffee. A true Montreal institution. (~$30–$40 CAD per person.)
meals.lunch: Premium gourmet picnic on Mont Royal — curated by your hotel concierge or sourced from the Plateau's finest artisan shops including La Fromagerie Hamel (cheeses) and Boucherie Lawrence (charcuterie). Pair with a chilled bottle of Quebec cider or French rosé.
meals.dinner: Joe Beef on Rue Notre-Dame Ouest — one of Canada's most celebrated and beloved restaurants. Known for its decadent, market-driven menu featuring whole lobster spaghetti, foie gras, and outstanding natural wine selections in a convivial, warm atmosphere. Reservations are essential and highly competitive — book weeks in advance. (~$120–$180 CAD per person.)

day_by_day.notes: Check local Plateau neighbourhood event listings via the Arrondissement du Plateau-Mont-Royal website for any specific street festivals happening this weekend. The Mont Royal picnic works best on a clear afternoon — check the morning forecast. Joe Beef reservations should be made as early as possible (they open bookings 30 days in advance online). Consider a backup reservation at Liverpool House next door (same ownership, equally excellent).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Old Montreal: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast. Afterward, visit the Marché Bonsecours (Bonsecours Market) for premium Quebec artisan goods, local designer boutiques, and handcrafted souvenirs — an ideal spot for last-minute luxury gifts. Stroll along the Vieux-Port waterfront one final time, taking in the views of the river and the historic architecture of Old Montreal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell Culinary Experience — Cooking Class or Chef's Table: Arrange a premium private Quebec cuisine cooking class or chef's table experience through your hotel concierge, learning to prepare classic dishes such as tourtière, maple-glazed duck, or poutine with high-end ingredients. Alternatively, visit the Atwater Market for a final gourmet stroll and tasting of Quebec products to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop or terrace restaurant with views over the city, celebrating the end of a perfect Montreal trip. Enjoy a curated Quebec wine and cocktail pairing as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or brunch at Crew Collective & Café in the stunning former Royal Bank of Canada building — a grand, architecturally magnificent space serving premium brunch fare including eggs Benedict, smoked salmon platters, and exceptional coffee in an awe-inspiring setting. (~$30–$45 CAD per person.)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Marché Bonsecours café or a curated tasting at Atwater Market — sample Quebec ice ciders, artisan honeys, fresh oysters, and local charcuterie for a relaxed, festive midday meal. (~$40–$60 CAD per person.)
meals.dinner: Hy's Steakhouse & Cocktail Bar Montreal or Rosélys at the Fairmont Queen Elizabeth — for the farewell dinner, opt for Rosélys' elegant seasonal Quebec-inspired tasting menu with an exceptional sommelier-curated wine pairing. The refined atmosphere and locally sourced ingredients make it a perfect celebratory final meal. (~$130–$180 CAD per person with wine pairing.)

day_by_day.notes: Check departure flight time and arrange a private luxury transfer back to Montreal-Trudeau Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Request a late checkout from Old Montreal Stay if your flight is in the evening — most luxury properties can accommodate this with advance notice. Marché Bonsecours is open daily and is a short walk from the hotel. Consider purchasing Quebec maple products, local cheeses (vacuum-sealed), and artisan spirits as premium take-home gifts.
